[deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] retry-loop-without-bounds -- The supervisor's main loop (while ($true)) has no bounded retry or circuit-breaker integration for the outer loop itself. If Start-Srv or Start-Drv consistently fail (e.g., due to a corrupt PowerShell installation or disk full), the supervisor will spin forever, spawning and killing processes in an unbounded tight loop (3-second sleep between iterations). This can cause resource exhaustion (process handle leak, log file bloat) and prevent manual recovery. | Recommend: Add a bounded retry counter with exponential backoff (e.g., max 10 consecutive failures, then exit with a fatal error message). Alternatively, integrate the existing circuit-breaker logic (Test-CircuitSpawnPaused) into the outer loop to pause spawning after repeated failures.
resolved_reason: fix(reliability): PID-tracking Kill-Bridge + bounded retry in supervisor -- closes c25a8e2d 34d52247 93d864f3 f5178f4c 7f775678

text: [deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] missing-cleanup -- The supervisor's Kill-Bridge function uses taskkill /F /T to kill all PowerShell processes matching server.ps1 or driver.ps1. This is a broad, non-atomic kill that can terminate unrelated PowerShell processes (e.g., user's own scripts, other bridge instances) if their command line happens to contain the substring. There is no PID tracking or process tree isolation. | Recommend: Track child process PIDs explicitly (store in $srv.Id and $drivers[$slug].Id) and kill only those specific PIDs with their process trees. Remove the wildcard Get-CimInstance + taskkill approach.
resolved_reason: fix(reliability): PID-tracking Kill-Bridge + bounded retry in supervisor -- closes c25a8e2d 34d52247 93d864f3 f5178f4c 7f775678

text: [deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] non-atomic-writes -- The supervisor writes to control/*.log files (supervisor.log, server.out.log, server.err.log, driver.*.log) using Out-File -Append. These writes are not atomic; a crash during write can produce partial lines or corrupt the log file. Multiple processes (supervisor + child processes) may write to the same log file concurrently, causing interleaved output. | Recommend: Use a logging function that writes to a dedicated log file per process with a mutex or use Windows EventLog for structured logging. Alternatively, use a single log file with a mutex (similar to Invoke-CircuitLogMutex in circuit-breaker.ps1).

[deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] brittle-process-supervision -- The supervisor uses Start-Process with -NoNewWindow -PassThru but does not monitor the child process's health (e.g., via process exit events or periodic health checks). It only checks $srv.HasExited and $proc.HasExited on each loop iteration (every ~3 seconds). A process that hangs (not exits) will never be detected as dead, and the supervisor will not restart it. | Recommend: Add a health-check mechanism: periodically verify the child process is responsive (e.g., check its main window handle, send a test request to the server API, or monitor its CPU/memory usage). If the process is unresponsive for N consecutive checks, kill and restart it.

[deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] timeout-bug -- The Invoke-RunbookProcess function has a hard-coded TimeoutMs of 15000 (15 seconds) for all runbook processes. This is too short for long-running operations (e.g., git clone, build, test suite) and will cause false-positive timeouts. The timeout is not configurable per operation. | Recommend: Make the timeout configurable per runbook step (e.g., via a parameter in the runbook definition) or use a much larger default (e.g., 5 minutes). Add a warning log when a timeout occurs.

[deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] missing-cleanup -- The Invoke-RunbookProcess function does not clean up the process if it times out. It calls $proc.Kill() but does not wait for the process to exit (WaitForExit is called with a 5-second timeout, but the result is piped to Out-Null). If the process does not terminate within 5 seconds, it becomes a zombie. Additionally, the stdout/stderr tasks are waited for only 1 second after kill, which may lose output. | Recommend: After Kill(), call $proc.WaitForExit() with a reasonable timeout (e.g., 10 seconds) and log a warning if the process does not exit. Ensure stdout/stderr tasks are completed before returning (use async/await or synchronous reads).
resolved_reason: fix(reliability): PID-tracking Kill-Bridge + bounded retry in supervisor -- closes c25a8e2d 34d52247 93d864f3 f5178f4c 7f775678

text: [deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] retry-loop-without-bounds -- The watchdog's main loop (while ($true)) has no bounded retry or exit condition. If the bridge root path ($b) becomes invalid or git.exe is missing, the watchdog will loop forever, logging errors every 2 minutes. This is a minor issue because the watchdog is designed to run indefinitely, but it could be improved with a fatal-exit after N consecutive critical errors. | Recommend: Add a consecutive-failure counter; after 10 consecutive critical errors (e.g., missing git.exe, cannot read auth.json), log a fatal message and exit the process to avoid silent log bloat.

[deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] non-atomic-writes -- The watchdog writes to control/watchdog.log using Out-File -Append. This is not atomic; a crash during write can produce partial lines. However, since the watchdog is a single process writing to a single log file, the risk is low. | Recommend: Consider using a mutex or a dedicated logging function that ensures atomic writes (e.g., write to a temp file and rename). [deep-agent/reliability-model/deepseek-v4-flash] brittle-process-supervision -- The Start-BridgeJob function launches a background PowerShell process but does not monitor its health after launch. The job is considered 'running' until the .done file appears. If the PowerShell process crashes or hangs without creating the .done file, the job will be stuck in 'running' state forever. There is no timeout mechanism for jobs. | Recommend: Add a job timeout (configurable, e.g., 1 hour default) and a periodic cleanup that kills and marks as failed any job that exceeds the timeout. Also, add a heartbeat mechanism (e.g., periodic timestamp updates in the .done file) to detect hung processes.

Alternatively, use a named mutex or event to verify the process identity more robustly.
